questions.stem: A receipt records the cited form for the quiz. What is the Italian plural of "letto"?
questions.explanation: The singular noun "letto" forms its plural as "letti". Italian nouns change their ending to mark number, and the article changes in tandem to agree with the new plural form.
questions.hint: Recall how nouns of this gender and ending form their plural.

questions.stem: While reading the passage, a learner flags one word during the exercise. What does Paolo dream of?

options.misconception: this detail is not supported by the passage and misreads it
this detail is not supported by the passage and misreads it
this detail is not supported by the passage and misreads it

questions.explanation: He dreams di aprire un piccolo ristorante. Read the surrounding context and the grammar of the sentence to confirm the choice.
questions.hint: Look for the infinitive after 'di'.

questions.subject: ITALIAN
questions.stem: A review lesson isolates the word for practice. Choose the subjunctive: "tu dire".

options.misconception: this is the noi form of the verb, not tu
this is the loro form of the verb, not tu
this is the voi form of the verb, not tu

questions.explanation: The subjunctive form of "dire" for "tu" is "dica". The present subjunctive is used after expressions of doubt, wish, or necessity. It draws its stem from the third-person plural present. Selecting the wrong person ending changes who performs the action.
questions.hint: Identify the subject pronoun, then apply the subjunctive ending for that person.

questions.subject: ITALIAN
questions.stem: Which definite article precedes the noun "scuola"?

options.misconception: used only before a vowel-initial word
reserved for z or s-plus-consonant words

questions.explanation: The noun "scuola" is feminine singular and begins with a consonant, so the definite article is "la". The other options belong to a different gender, number, or sound class.
questions.hint: Check the noun's gender and its first sound before choosing the article.

questions.subject: ITALIAN
questions.learningObjective: Identify the infinitive behind a conjugated form
questions.stem: Which infinitive does the form "ricevevano" come from?
questions.explanation: The form "ricevevano" is the imperfect form for "loro" of "ricevere". Identifying the infinitive behind a conjugated form requires matching the stem and the person endings to the correct conjugation pattern.
questions.hint: Strip the ending and match the remaining stem to an infinitive.
